newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY FIRMS, DEPOS RISE ON RATES RISE EXPECTATIONS.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY FIRMS, DEPOS RISE ON RATES RISE EXPECTATIONS.

text.p: The Polish zloty firmed against the basket of currencies to around -1.0 percent from parity and short- and long-term deposits rates rose as the central bank announced it would soon raise its nominal rates, dealers said.
"T/N rates rose on the NBP chief statement, and the same goes for long-term rates, especially for one month deposits," said Wojciech Kolasinski, a debt dealer at Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA.
Players said they were now waiting for the actual rate rise, which they said could happen any time, despite the several weeks horizon set by the central bank.

Dealers said that after an early bout of zloty purchases on the back of the NBP interest rate remarks the forex market stabilised and would likely wait for the move to happen before foreign players would consider entering the market.
"The foreign players are waiting for the official interest rates increase and investment's profitability rise," said Dorota Alender, a forex dealer at BIG SA.

But some said the zloty would not see much stabilisation until after parliamentary polls on September 21. "The zloty rate will most likely keep swinging until the elections," Marek Golebiewski, a forex dealer at PBK SA, said.
On the money market T/N bids jumped to 24 percent with no offers and overnight rates were expected to join them tomorrow, when the new, August reserve period starts, dealers said.
"As for long-term deposits, the situation may be described as a rush for money, since one-month deposits were offered at above 25 percent," Wojciech Kolasinski said.

O/N rates closed at 2.00/5.00 percent against around 1.00 at opening. Tomorrow/next were at 23.91/24.97 percent against 24.20/24.90 percent at opening. The central bank sold 227 million of its 91-bills.
